name: Animate UI
license: MIT + Commons Clause (GitHub SPDX: NOASSERTION; LICENSE.md)
install: npx shadcn@latest add @animate-ui/<slug>  (e.g. npx shadcn@latest add @animate-ui/primitives-texts-sliding-number; pnpm dlx / yarn / bunx variants documented)
stack: shadcn CLI registry distribution (copy-into-project, no npm runtime package)
Radix UI / Base UI / Headless UI variants
notes: Verification: animate-ui.com footer links to github.com/imskyleen; canonical repo is imskyleen/animate-ui (owner Elliot Sutton, ~4.2k stars, active, last push 2025-12-31, homepage=animate-ui.com; github.com/animate-ui/animate-ui redirects there). SalarC123/Animate-UI from the task brief returns 404 - not this project. License caveat: LICENSE.md is MIT plus a Commons Clause-style restriction - free to use, copy, modify and distribute the code as part of an app/site/product (commercial use allowed), but you may NOT sell or redistribute the components themselves in original form, alone or in a bundle. It is source-available and free to copy, but not OSI open-source; fine for a personal catalog app, do not resell the components as a component library. Distribution: shadcn-style registry, not an npm package - each item installs via 'npx shadcn@latest add @animate-ui/<slug>'; registry JSON at https://animate-ui.com/r/<slug>.json. Total count: 154 documented animated components = 73 'Components' + 81 'Primitives' (verified 1:1 against registry items and docs MDX files; complete, not sampled). category format is '<Section> / <sidebar group>' - the library's own top-level split (Components vs Primitives) plus its sidebar heading; both sections have Animate UI / Radix UI / Base UI / Headless UI / Buttons groups, so the section prefix disambiguates duplicates (e.g. two Tabs). Also in the registry but not enumerated here (no individual docs pages): 260 animated Lucide icons (beta) and 5 hooks (use-auto-height, use-controlled-state, use-data-state, use-is-in-view, use-motion-value-state). Docs also document an MCP server (animate-ui.com/docs/mcp). Community components are user-contributed via the repo.
